target_customer: VR content creators, robotics and film teams needing 3D volumetric video
problem: Standard VR video causes motion sickness because it lacks depth and head motion; volumetric video needs heavy ML processing.
business_model: Software tools and editor, with open source players

founders.name: Forrest Briggs
education: PhD in machine learning (institution not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page; lists 20+ patents. Search result says a co-founder existed, unnamed; not recorded.

competitors.name: Facebook (Surround 360 six degrees of freedom cameras)
Google (light field volumetric video)
competitors.what: Light field capture and streaming for 6DOF video

technical_complexity.rationale: Neural reconstruction of per-frame 3D from VR180 footage and a new ldi3 format is near research grade for two people.

defensibility.rationale: ML expertise from Facebook VR cameras is hard to copy but the tools are open sourced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Meta and Google had built similar capture research earlier; no acquisition of Lifecast found.

market_need_then: VR video motion sickness was a known comfort problem per the YC description; mass VR video demand was limited.

branding.domain_note: Uses lifecastvr.com, a prefixed domain; it now redirects to GitHub.

brand_strength.rationale: A product launched on Product Hunt in 2023 and Leia covered the Volurama tool; the name also means body-molding sculpture, which adds search noise.

pivots.to: Volumetric video editor and open source players
pivots.why: Product Hunt launch date; reason not found

outcome_analysis: The cause of the inactive status is not public: no shutdown post, post-mortem or press report was found. Lifecast built ML-driven volumetric video tools in a VR market that stayed small, raised only a small amount around YC, and shipped a volumetric editor in 2023. Dealroom marks it closed and the website now redirects to its GitHub repository.
notes: The $500K pre-seed rests on one directory (the search listed several; I attributed it to VC Backed unverified). Crunchbase returned 403. Product Hunt date of the editor is September 2023.
